clues: It sits on the Rhine River in Germany, at the foot of the Taunus hills. Mainz lies just across the stream, a state capital too.
High hills shield it from the north and west. So this basin town stays mild, and folks call it the Nice of the North.
In 1806, it became the capital of the Duchy of Nassau. Its new palace, built in 1841, was the chief home of its dukes.
It is one of the old spa towns of Europe. Fifteen springs bubble up in its heart, and all but one pour out hot.
Each day its springs pour out two million liters of water. No spa town in all of Germany beats it but one.
